     4	Fix translation bugs and an error mapping bug in the bridge service that translates

     7	## Requirements
     8	1. int64 fields must be translated as Python int (no truncation to 32-bit)

    15	- `service_b/schema.py` — Message schema for Service B (proto3-style)
    16	- `bridge/translator.py` — JSON→Message translation
    17	- `bridge/error_mapper.py` — HTTP status → error code
    18	
    19	## Background
    20	
    21	The bridge service sits between Service A (a REST API returning JSON) and Service B
    22	(a queue consumer expecting structured proto3-style messages). Because JSON and proto3
    23	have different type semantics, every field crossing this boundary needs a careful
    24	type conversion.
    25

    27	
    28	| JSON Type | Proto3 Type | Issue |
    29	|-----------|-------------|-------|
    30	| number    | int64       | JSON numbers lose precision for values > 2^53; must not be masked to 32-bit |
    31	| string    | bytes       | Binary data is base64-encoded in JSON; must be decoded to bytes |
    32

    35	Service A returns HTTP status codes. Service B uses gRPC-style integer error codes:
    36	
    37	| HTTP Status | Expected Error Code | Code Number |

    40	| 400         | INVALID_ARGUMENT    | 3           |
    41	| 401/403     | INVALID_ARGUMENT    | 3           |
    42	| 404         | NOT_FOUND           | 5           |
    43	| 5xx         | INTERNAL            | 13          |

    47	architectures, and the bugs in this task reflect bugs documented in real transcoding
